For every nontrivial finite-dimensional real inner-product space E, every 0<alpha<1, and every natural T satisfying T>=2/((1-alpha)*phi(alpha)), there exists a horizon-dependent sequence of globally convex, 1-Lipschitz, differentiable real losses. The SAME actual OnlineGradientDescent.iterateVariable/regretVariable run on fullSpace starts at zero and compares with zero, with source eta_t=t^(-alpha).
ALGORITHM PARAMETERS
Lean loss index t is source round t+1; eta(t)=(t+1)^(-alpha), state0=x1=0, and loss t is scored at state t before updating to state(t+1). Comparator0 is unchanged. Existing phi_range and phi_limit remain separate accepted OSD supplements, not new direct proof parents of this terminal.
REGRET NOTION
R_T(0)=sum_{t=1}^T (loss_t(x_t)-loss_t(0)); exact factor1/2, zero initial point and comparator.
GUARANTEE
Choose a unit vector v and m=ceil(T/2). Let loss_t(z)=-<v,z> for source t<=m and +<v,z> thereafter. Each loss is globally differentiable, convex and 1-Lipschitz. Its actual gradient and the canonical OSD selected subgradient both equal the signed unit vector. Induction identifies the two actual trajectories at every time; their pre-update regret sums agree. Apply the accepted switching_vector_lower_bound to obtain the same exact half-phi bound. The loss stream may depend on T; no fixed infinite witness or Tendsto theorem is asserted.

Intuition
Larger early steps move the learner along a unit direction; after the affine slope switches halfway through, smaller later steps make the return too slow. The proof tracks the actual gradient trajectory.
